report.summary: Chunk 9 of 11: implements promotion loop, cleanup, and run_write_wave function with governance check.
risks: run_write_wave | medium | assignments parameter must be in same order as tasks; mismatch could cause silent misclassification. | Check that caller guarantees order consistency and that length check is performed.
cancel parameter | low | cancel is forwarded to gate_candidates but not visible in this chunk; its effect depends on external implementation. | Verify that gate_candidates respects cancel.
cleanup_error | low | Exception in cleanup_worktree is caught and stored, but reap_branches exception is silently ignored. | Consider whether ignoring reap_branches exceptions is safe.
governance_verdict | medium | Imports daedalus.core.get_governance; if unavailable, returns unknown state. | Ensure daedalus.core is installed and accessible.

auto_promote | low | AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS = ("never",) but parameter still exists; legacy values cannot reach promote_candidates. | Verify that legacy values are indeed filtered out before this function.
todos: Verify that assignments parameter is length-checked against tasks before use.
Ensure that cleanup_worktree and reap_branches are safe to call even after partial promotion.
Confirm that cancel parameter is correctly forwarded to all concurrent attempts.

handoff.purpose: Promotion loop, cleanup, and run_write_wave function with governance integration.

symbols.name: promote_candidates
symbols.note: Promotes candidates to integration branch, handles cleanup, returns report.

symbols.name: _governance_verdict
symbols.note: Returns (promotion_allowed, governance_state, headline) by calling daedalus.core.get_governance.

symbols.name: run_write_wave
symbols.note: Executes write-mode tasks through gated worktree path, holds candidates for explicit promotion.

claims.text: ``cancel``, when given, is forwarded to ``gate_candidates`` for every concurrent attempt in this wave.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the implementation of gate_candidates or how cancel is forwarded.

claims.text: ``None`` (the default) is byte-identical to this function's behaviour before ``cancel`` existed
claims.why: The chunk does not show previous behavior or default handling.

claims.text: A caller driving a longer-lived loop ... can pass one shared token/``KillSwitch`` here so a stop request reaches every in-flight ``TaskAttempt`` and every in-flight cumulative gate this wave started
claims.why: The chunk does not show how cancel is used or propagated.

claims.text: ``assignments`` MUST be ``scheduler.accept(tasks, repo_root=repo_root)``'s own return, in the SAME order as ``tasks``
claims.why: The chunk does not include the implementation that uses assignments; it only declares the parameter.

claims.text: Recomputing it here would still be SAFE (``accept`` is a pure classification -- no persona-cycling or other per-call state feeds it; two calls on the same tasks always agree)
claims.why: The chunk does not show scheduler.accept implementation or its purity.

claims.text: Non-write tasks in the SAME wave (advisory, or bounced to the senior lane) are NOT touched by the gated path: they are delegated back to ``scheduler.dispatch``, scoped to just their own indices
claims.why: The chunk ends before showing that delegation.

claims.text: ``_governance_verdict`` -- read straight off ``daedalus.core.get_governance``, never re-derived here.
claims.why: The function calls get_governance and returns its values directly.

claims.text: Any failure to even ASK the question -- ``daedalus.core`` unimportable, the call itself raising -- reports the vocabulary's ``unknown``, not a silent True.
claims.why: Both import failure and call failure return False and 'unknown'.

claims.text: ``unknown`` and ``absent`` stay distinct facts (see ``daedalus.core.GOVERNANCE_STATES``): this only ever manufactures ``unknown`` for a failure that happened HERE; a real ``absent`` receipt is already reported correctly by ``get_governance`` itself and passes through unchanged.
claims.why: The chunk does not show daedalus.core.GOVERNANCE_STATES or get_governance's behavior for 'absent'.

claims.text: The only production-capable value is "never"; legacy values cannot reach ``promote_candidates``.
claims.why: The chunk does not show how legacy values are filtered before reaching this function.

observations.what: promote_candidates returns report with promoted/refused lists and cleanup_error if any.
cleanup_error is set if cleanup_worktree raises, but reap_branches exception is silently ignored.
AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS is a tuple with single value 'never'; parameter auto_promote still accepted but not used in this chunk.
_governance_verdict catches import and call exceptions, returns False and 'unknown'.
run_write_wave docstring references scheduler.accept and scheduler.dispatch but these are not shown in this chunk.
